questions.question: An engineer needs to analyse signal strength in communications cabling over time. Describe a device that the engineer could use in testing signal strength.

Sample answer:
One device that could be used is a cathode ray oscilloscope (CRO) which can be used for

questions.name: Question 21 (b)
questions.question: Explain why aluminium alloy wire is used as an electrical transmission medium between communications towers.

questionContent.text: Explain why aluminium alloy wire is used as an electrical transmission medium between communications towers.

questions.answer:
Use the following NESA marking criteria and sample answer. Accept equivalent correct engineering reasoning and working; do not require the sample wording. Only credit evidence present in the submitted response. Never assume an unsubmitted drawing or calculation is correct.
• Explains why aluminium alloy wire is used as an electrical transmission
3
medium
• Outlines relevant features of aluminium alloy wire 2
• Provides some relevant information 1
Sample answer:
Aluminium is commonly used in transmission lines because its low density allows it to better
support its own weight over long spans, reducing sag and enabling wider tower spacing. This
makes infrastructure more economical with fewer towers required in the transmission
network. Aluminium is also less expensive than copper and more abundant in nature.

questions.name: Question 21 (c)
questions.question: Explain how voice signals are transmitted between two mobile phones over a cellular mobile network. Use a labelled sketch to support your answer.

questionContent.text: Explain how voice signals are transmitted between two mobile phones over a cellular mobile network. Use a labelled sketch to support your answer.

questions.answer:
Use the following NESA marking criteria and sample answer. Accept equivalent correct engineering reasoning and working; do not require the sample wording. Only credit evidence present in the submitted response. Never assume an unsubmitted drawing or calculation is correct.
• Explains how voice signals are transmitted between mobile phones

• Explains how voice signals are transmitted between mobile phones
OR 2

Sample answer:
When a person speaks into Phone A, the microphone converts sound waves into electrical
signals, which are then digitised and modulated into a radio frequency (RF) signal. This
signal is transmitted to the nearest cell base station and then through the ground station. The
signal is then transmitted via satellite to the other ground station, and on to the Phone B cell
base station to be demodulated and converted back to sound waves at Phone B.

questions.question: A building is being partially demolished and replaced. Part of the original structure will be retained. Outline a method that could be used to recycle a material from the building.

questionContent.text: A building is being partially demolished and replaced. Part of the original structure will be retained. Outline a method that could be used to recycle a material from the building.

Use the following NESA marking criteria and sample answer. Accept equivalent correct engineering reasoning and working; do not require the sample wording. Only credit evidence present in the submitted response. Never assume an unsubmitted drawing or calculation is correct.

• Provides some relevant information 1
Sample answer:
Concrete from demolished structures can be crushed and recycled as aggregate for new
construction projects, reducing waste.
Answers could include:
Steel from demolished structures (roofing, foundations, framing and fences) can be melted
down and reused in new construction, reducing the demand for raw materials.
Glass (windows, skylights, backsplashes, shower screens, mirrors, light fixtures) can be
crushed into cullet and recycled into new glass products or used as aggregate in concrete or

Describe a suitable process which could be used to detect surface cracks in ONE steel component of the building.

questionContent.text: A building is being partially demolished and replaced. Part of the original structure will be retained. Engineers want to retain some steel components of the building. Describe a suitable process which could be used to detect surface cracks in ONE steel component of the building.

Use the following NESA marking criteria and sample answer. Accept equivalent correct engineering reasoning and working; do not require the sample wording. Only credit evidence present in the submitted response. Never assume an unsubmitted drawing or calculation is correct.
• Describes a suitable process for detecting surface cracks in one steel

• Identifies some features of a process for detecting surface cracks in one
2

• Provides some relevant information 1
Sample answer:
Dye penetrant testing can be used for detecting surface cracks in steel brackets. It involves
cleaning the steel, applying a liquid dye that penetrates any surface cracks, and allowing it to
settle. After wiping off the excess dye, a developer is applied, drawing the dye out of cracks,
making them visible under ultraviolet light. The cracks are then inspected for severity.
Answers could include:
• Magnetic particle inspection
• Visual inspection
• Eddy current testing.

questions.name: Question 24 (c)
questions.question: Describe the operation of a mechanical altimeter. Use a labelled diagram to support your answer.

questionContent.text: Describe the operation of a mechanical altimeter. Use a labelled diagram to support your answer.

questions.answer:
Use the following NESA marking criteria and sample answer. Accept equivalent correct engineering reasoning and working; do not require the sample wording. Only credit evidence present in the submitted response. Never assume an unsubmitted drawing or calculation is correct.
• Describes the operation of a mechanical altimeter
4

• Outlines the operation of a mechanical altimeter
3
• Includes a relevant labelled diagram
• Describes the operation of a mechanical altimeter
OR 2
• Provides a relevant labelled sketch
• Provides some relevant information 1
Sample answer:
An altimeter operates by measuring changes in atmospheric pressure as altitude changes. It
uses a sealed capsule (aneroid) that responds to external air pressure. As the altitude
increases, the external pressure connected to the static vent decreases, causing the sealed
capsule to expand. This expansion is mechanically linked to a needle or a digital display,
which indicates the altitude. The greater the altitude, the greater the expansion of the sealed
capsule due to lower air pressure around the capsule.

Sample answer:
Pre-tensioned concrete involves tensioning tendons before pouring the concrete, typically in
a factory. It requires less time on-site and is cost-effective for mass production.
Post-tensioned concrete involves tensioning tendons after curing the concrete, usually
onsite, offering flexibility but requiring more time, equipment, and potentially higher costs.

questions.question: A truss is loaded as shown. Determine the magnitude and nature of the force in member M.

questionContent.text: A truss is loaded as shown.
Determine the magnitude and nature of the force in member M.

questions.answer:
Use the following NESA marking criteria and sample answer. Accept equivalent correct engineering reasoning and working; do not require the sample wording. Only credit evidence present in the submitted response. Never assume an unsubmitted drawing or calculation is correct.
• Calculates the magnitude of the force and states its nature 6

5
force and states its nature
• Makes some progress towards calculating the magnitude 3–4
• Provides some relevant calculation 2
• Provides some relevant information 1
Sample answer:
Transcription of the graphical sample solution: the truss has a 9 kN downward load and a 15 kN load at 60° to the horizontal, span 2800 mm, height 700 mm and half-span 1400 mm. θ = atan(700/1400) = 26.565°. Taking moments about A: R_B = (9×1.4 + 15sin60°×2.8 − 15cos60°×0.7)/2.8 = 15.615 kN upward. On the right side of a section through member M, vertical equilibrium gives F_M sinθ = 15.615 − 15sin60° = 2.625 kN. F_M = 5.8697 kN = 5869.7 N, in tension. These are equivalent units; accept sensible rounding and alternative valid methods. The final line of the printed sample has an inconsistent unit rendering; use 5.8697 kN or 5869.7 N.

heated to a specific temperature after being rapidly cooled from a high temperature, allowing
